ai.description: *Megophrys serchhipii* is a small toad (32–36 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark, triangular markings. It features prominent, fleshy supraocular horns and a distinct, dark-edged tympanum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys serchhipii* is best distinguished by its unique, narrow, and elongated "horn" on the upper eyelid, which is significantly longer than those of other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys serchhipii* inhabits the subtropical broadleaf forests of Mizoram, India, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Megophrys serchhipii is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush small invertebrates while avoiding detection by potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys serchhipii* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in forest streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys serchhipii* is endemic to the state of Mizoram in Northeast India, where it inhabits high-elevation montane forests.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Megophrys serchhipii* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from near streams in dense forest habitats.
